items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to paperwork reduction; to amend the education law, in relation to the streamlining of planning and reporting requirements for school districts and boards of cooperative educational services; requiring the commissioner of education to implement pilot programs to assist school districts in the formation of regional transportation systems; to repeal subdivision 32 of section 305 of the education law relating to reviews by the commissioner; and to repeal section 805 of the education law relating to enforcement provisions for the willful refusal to teach certain subjects; and providing for the repeal of certain provisions upon expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S8376

TITLE OF BILL:

An act
to amend the education law, in relation to paperwork reduction; to amend
the education law, in relation to the streamlining of planning and
reporting requirements for school districts and boards of cooperative
educational services; requiring the commissioner of education to
implement pilot programs to assist school districts in the formation of
regional transportation systems; to repeal subdivision 32 of section 305
of the education law relating to reviews by the commissioner; and to
repeal section 805 of the education law relating to enforcement
provisions for the willful refusal to teach certain subjects; and
providing for the repeal of certain provisions upon expiration
thereof

PURPOSE:

This bill would authorize the commissioner of education to accept
reports electronically, require a report on the reduction or
consolidation of reports by school districts, alter certain reporting
requirements placed on school districts and Boards of Cooperative
Educational Services (BOCES) and authorize the establishment of
regional transportation pilot programs.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill authorizes the Commissioner of Education to
accept reports and all other required information electronically,
except in cases where submitting electronically would be an undue
hardship for a school district. It would also direct the Commissioner
to prepare a report by November 1, 2010 recommending ways that
reporting and planning requirements could be eliminated or
consolidated, statutorily or administratively.

Section 2 of the bill would repeal Education Law §305 (32), which
called for a 2002 report on the number of reports filed by school
districts.

Section 3 of the bill would repeal Education Law §805, which requires
the suspension of a teacher's license and the withholding of all
state aid from a school district if it is found that any teacher has
willfully failed to teach health education (as required by Education
Law §804) until multiple investigations are conducted.

Section 4 of the bill amends Education Law §2802 (5) to require
reports on school violence to be submitted by April 1 instead of
January 1 and to change how the levels of violence in schools and
districts are analyzed to ensure that like schools and districts are
compared.

Section 5 of the bill would amend Education Law § 1950(4)(b)(5) to
eliminate an outdated requirement for BOCES to separate its program,
capital and administrative costs for the 1994-1995 school year budget.

Section 6 of the bill would amend Education Law § 1950 (4)(c) to
continue the requirement that BOCES prepare long range program plans,
including special education and career education plans, but removes
the required submission to the State Department of Education. Instead
the bill would require the plan to be on file and available for
public inspection and review by the Commissioner. This section would
eliminate the requirement that BOCES submit sections of the plan
pertaining to special education and career education programs every
two years provided that such plans may be incorporated into a BOCES
district-wide comprehensive plan.

Section 7 of the bill would amend Education Law § 1950 (4) (kk)
concerning the BOCES report card. The amendment would delete
reference to including in the report card specific information
included in the Regents annual report to the Governor and the
Legislature pursuant to Education Law § 215-a. The Commissioner would
continue to have the responsibility to provide certain information
needed to ensure the accountability of BOCES pursuant to Education
Law § 215-b.

Section 8 of the bill would amend Education Law § 3602 (11) (f) to
eliminate the requirement that school districts and BOCES submit a
plan of service and evaluation for approval of the Commissioner, in
order to receive aid for Employment Preparation programs. The
amendment would continue to require submission of an annual
application for the payment of aid, to be approved by the Commissioner.

Section 9 of the bill would amend Education Law § 3602(8) (b) to fully
eliminate the requirement that school districts submit to the
Commissioner plans of service for three categorical aid programs and
to replace such requirement with a requirement that the district
plans of service be kept on file and available for public inspection.

Section 10 of the bill authorizes and directs the Commissioner of
Education to conduct one or more pilot programs to assist interested
school districts in the formation of regional transportation systems.
It further directs the Commissioner of Education to report on
participation in the pilot programs on each November 1 and to report
on November 1, 2012 the potential for efficiencies,
cost-effectiveness, and cost savings to be gained by implementing
regional transportation systems, as well as barriers to
implementation and recommendations for effective oversight of such
systems.

Section 11 of the bill provides the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

To reduce the paperwork burden on school districts, BOCES, and the
State Education Department, this bill authorizes the Commissioner of
Education to accept reports, plans, and other required submissions
electronically. It also directs the Commissioner to determine which
reporting requirements can be eliminated or consolidated, and to
identify which of those changes would need to be made statutorily. It
is anticipated that that report will provide a roadmap for future
bills adopting the Commissioner's recommendations.

This bill starts the process of eliminating or streamlining various
specific reporting requirements currently imposed by statute. It
streamlines a series of reporting requirements currently imposed on
BOCES, while maintaining oversight over the related programs. Now
more than ever, it is important that school districts have the
ability to direct resources toward their core educational missions,
rather than duplicative administrative burdens.

Authorizing the study of the benefits of, and impediments to regional
transportation, will allow SED to examine the long term viability and
cost effectiveness of these collaborative services.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

The bill will create no additional cost to the state or school
districts. It will produce savings in staff time, printing and
mailing at the state and local levels for preparing and reviewing
separate and, in many instances, duplicative information
requirements. The exact amount of the savings is difficult to
estimate as the time required to comply varies widely among school
districts. It will also most likely produce savings for the districts
that choose to participate in the regional transportation pilot
program, as districts will likely not choose to participate unless
they anticipate savings.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
The bill would take effect immediately; provided, however, that the
commissioner of education shall promulgate any rules or regulations
necessary to implement the provisions of this act on or before July
1, 2010; provided further that if section ten of this act shall take
effect after July 1, 2010 it shall be deemed to have been in full
force and effect on and after July 1, 2010; and provided further that
section ten of this act shall expire and be deemed repealed on June
30, 2015.

summary: Relates to paperwork reduction; streamlines planning and reporting requirements for school districts and boards of cooperative educational services; requires the commissioner of education to implement pilot programs to assist school districts in the formation of regional transportation systems.
